GruntWorx should inherit Instead’s reliability patterns and shared TaxAutomations infrastructure, with its own adapter for vendor-specific limits, statuses and identity rules.

1. **Rate limits: budget every API exchange.** Instead enforces both an app-wide RPM limit and a per-connection, per-API-group limit. The group check runs first so rejected work does not consume the app budget; unknown groups fall back to `default`. Workers generally perform at most one vendor exchange, and HTTP 429 respects `Retry-After`, including HTTP-date values. Keep this structure, but obtain GruntWorx’s actual limits and scope. Instead’s development and production budgets already differ—copying its numbers would be unsafe. Sources: [throttle configuration](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/config/initializers/sidekiq.rb:101), [shared worker](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/workers/tax_preparation/tax_automations/operation_worker.rb:3).

2. **Lost webhooks: provide a bounded reconciliation path from day one.** Current defaults select uploaded documents still `sent` after one hour or `processing` after twelve hours, looking back two days. Instead groups reads by entity/year, paginates folder listings, then individually fetches candidates absent from all pages: a file may have moved. Only an individual document 404 becomes `archived`; a missing folder or inaccessible entity is skipped. Reconciliation uses a low-priority throttled queue and the same status application service as webhooks, making repeated reports harmless and preventing invalid backward transitions. Preserve these properties, while choosing GruntWorx-specific thresholds and lookup APIs. **Existing limitation:** older documents are left unchanged after the two-day window. Sources: [candidate selection](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/queries/tax_preparation/tax_automations/documents/reconcile_candidates_query.rb:8), [fallback lookup](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/services/tax_preparation/tax_automations/instead/documents/reconcile_status.rb:3), [status application](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/services/tax_preparation/tax_automations/instead/documents/apply_processing_status.rb:3).

3. **Failure reasons: preserve a small, actionable product vocabulary.** Shared reasons are `unexpected`, `no_active_connection`, `network_error`, `unauthorized`, `api_error`, `exceeded`, `forbidden`, and `encrypted`. Map vendor errors by meaning: temporary throttling retries; exhausted plan quota becomes `exceeded`; invalid grants become `unauthorized`; policy denials become `forbidden`; remaining terminal API refusals generally become `api_error`. Instead maps `password_required` to `encrypted`; unknown processing-failure reasons remain unspecified. Give GruntWorx its own explicit mapping, retaining vendor diagnostics separately. Keep upload failure distinct from processing failure, and ensure retry exhaustion ends affected uploads. Sources: [failure vocabulary](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/models/tax_preparation/tax_automations/document.rb:15), [refusal handling](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/lib/tax_preparation/tax_automations/refusals_helper.rb:8).

4. **Signed-URL cassettes: scrub capabilities and preserve expiry semantics.** Instead’s tests replay real API exchanges and freeze time at the cassette’s first recording timestamp, so recorded upload targets do not become artificially expired. Global recording hooks scrub S3 policy, credential and signature fields while preserving response shape. **A second vendor needs additional coverage:** bearer/token scrubbing currently depends on the Instead hostname, and these hooks do not sanitize signed URL query parameters. Extend sanitization for GruntWorx’s actual authentication and upload format before recording it. Sources: [recording hooks](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/spec/spec_helper.rb:164), [fixed-time replay](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/spec/support/vcr_fixed_time.rb:3).

5. **Entity matching: reuse persistent identity before attempting names.** Instead first finds an existing active link by firm/account/contact/entity type, shared across tax years; then attempts conservative name matching; then creates an entity. Name matching considers only active, unlinked entities of the correct type and accepts exactly one candidate. It normalizes punctuation, whitespace and case, supports business legal-form spellings, and tries swapped personal names only after no direct match. Account-name fallback for individuals requires a sole contact. Ambiguous matches never select arbitrarily. Preserve tenant isolation, ambiguity handling and durable vendor IDs; validate GruntWorx’s identity model before reusing these exact rules. Instead’s entity creation is explicitly non-idempotent, so duplicate prevention deserves particular attention. Sources: [workflow](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/workers/tax_preparation/tax_automations/instead/documents/export_async_workflow.rb:26), [matching rules](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/services/tax_preparation/tax_automations/instead/clients/link_entity_by_name.rb:3).

This is based on source and test inspection. No files were edited; tests were not run.
